title: AM, FM and PM: what changes
idea: Modulation puts information onto RF by changing one thing about it. AM changes the amplitude, FM the frequency, PM the phase. FSK flips between two frequencies.

rows: Instantaneous power (amplitude); the envelope joins the peaks
Phase angle; a reactance modulator on an RF amp makes it
Oscillator frequency switched by a digital signal
Scope vertical input: attenuated RF output

compare.how: Amplitude: the instantaneous power level changes.

traps.why: A reactance modulator shifts the phase: phase modulation.
No such name. Varying the power level is amplitude modulation.

traps.wrong: The bandwidth of the modulated signal
traps.why: The envelope is the line joining the peaks.

traps.wrong: The local oscillator of the transmitter
traps.why: You look at what comes out: the attenuated RF output.
